title: Vladimir's envoys (988)
hookLine: Kyiv's prince sends envoys to find a faith; at Hagia Sophia they didn't know if they were in heaven or on earth
tomorrow: Block close: the first thousand years

cards: Some travelers come home from a long trip and can't stop talking. Others come home and struggle to find words at all. A chronicle from Kyiv tells of a few men who came home the second way.
Their prince, Vladimir, had sent them out to see how different peoples worshiped. At last they reached Constantinople, the city of the great church we stood under five days ago.
When they returned and tried to describe it, what came out was not a report. It was a confession of being lost for words.

teach.b: The story comes from the Primary Chronicle, a history written in Kyiv later, by monks looking back.

It says Vladimir received visitors from several peoples, each describing their faith, then sent his own envoys to see for themselves. We'll leave aside what the chronicle has them say about each place.
What it remembers most is Constantinople. The Greeks, it says, led the envoys into the church where they worship their God.

teach.h: HEAVEN OR EARTH? WE DID NOT KNOW.
teach.b: And the envoys reported, in paraphrase: we did not know whether we were in heaven or on earth. There is no such splendor or beauty anywhere on earth, and we cannot describe it.
We only know that God dwells there among people. We cannot forget that beauty. That's the heart of it.
Not an argument. An experience of worship.
In the chronicle's telling, Vladimir was baptized, and then the people of Kyiv were called down to the river and baptized together in the Dnieper.
Historians read the chronicle carefully; it was written later, and it shapes the story. Christians in Ukraine, Russia and Belarus look back to that baptism as a beginning. There's an older echo.

teach.h: THIS IS THE GATE OF HEAVEN.
teach.b: Jacob, in Genesis, wakes from a dream at Bethel and says, in the King James words: "How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."
The same astonishment: a place on earth that felt like heaven's doorway. Jacob set up a stone to mark it. The envoys carried home a sentence.

how: Orthodox Christians in Ukraine, Russia and Belarus remember the baptism of Kyiv and Saint Vladimir, and Orthodox worship gives great care to beauty: icons, chant, incense and light.

o: a long report on their teaching.
we did not know whether we were in heaven or on earth.
games.why: the chronicle has them confess they couldn't describe it: only that God dwells there among people.

practice: Step slowly into a beautiful place near you, a garden, a doorway, a kitchen with good light, as if you'd traveled a long way to get there, or walk into one you remember with your eyes closed.
Notice the light, then the sound, then the smell, and let it be bigger than your words. If you pray, let Jacob's line sit with you; if you don't, just stay inside the beauty a while.

wordCard.voice: Vladimir's envoys. The men a prince of Kyiv sent to see how others worshiped, who said that in Constantinople they did not know whether they were in heaven or on earth.

carryVoice: Your line: heaven or earth? Sometimes beauty says what an argument can't. See you soon.
